Commentary.Commentary: We are back with Bangladesh's reply! The umpires are out and so are the players of the Indian team who head out in the field after a final pep talk from skipper Suryakumar Yadav in a huddle. Litton Das and Parvez Hossain Emon are the openers striding out for Bangladesh! It will be Arshdeep Singh to start the proceedings for India with the new ball in hand. Away we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

This isn't the usual Delhi batting paradise, and Bangladesh will need to start strong to have any chance of chasing down this mammoth total. While the dew hasn't settled in yet, if it does, it could pose significant challenges for the Indian bowlers which makes the first 6 overs crucial for both sides. Sit back and enjoy the second essay, which promises to be an exciting one!

Hardik Pandya joined forces with Rinku Singh, and together they unleashed a blistering partnership of 64 runs in just 21 balls, highlighting the carnage at the crease. Amidst the mayhem, Taskin Ahmed stood tall for Bangladesh, breaking the partnership and finishing with exceptional figures of 2 for just 16 runs in his 4 overs. Rinku also notched up a well-deserved half-century before being dismissed. Riyan Parag then stepped in, smashing a few quick boundaries, while Hardik continued to push India past the 200-run mark. However, Rishad Hossain was able to finish well, as India lost 3 wickets for just 8 runs, closing the innings on a dramatic note but with the scoreboard reading 221/9!

At 45/3 after the Powerplay, India found themselves in a precarious position. Nitish Kumar Reddy, starting cautiously, found a reliable ally in Rinku Singh, who began striking boundaries with ease from the moment he arrived at the crease. However, once Nitish found his rhythm, Rinku took a backseat, allowing Nitish the majority of the strike. Nitish went on an aggressive spree, reaching his maiden half-century in just 27 balls. Together, the duo stitched a rapid 108-run partnership, setting the stage for a big finish before Nitish was eventually dismissed by Mustafizur Rahman.

A decent end for Bangladesh, reining India in that last over as they wrap their innings at 221/9. After being asked to bat first, India got off to a flying start, capitalizing on the opening over. However, Bangladesh's captain Najmul Hossain Shanto quickly introduced his ace pacer, Taskin Ahmed, who expertly varied his pace and struck with the first breakthrough, dismissing Sanju Samson. Abhishek Sharma showed positive intent and looked to keep the momentum going but couldn't build on his start, falling in the very next over to a fierce delivery from Tanzim Hasan Sakib. Najmul's decision to trust his pace attack paid off again, as Mustafizur Rahman claimed another wicket inside the Powerplay, this time the dangerous Suryakumar Yadav, helping Bangladesh finish the powerplay on a strong note.

A single to end the innings! Rishad offers flight, full and on off, Mayank Yadav reaches out and smears it along the ground to long on and takes a single. An eventful final over. Three wickets and 8 runs off it. India finish with 221 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Despite losing three early wickets in the powerplay, this new duo of Nitish Kumar Reddy and Rinku Singh has shifted momentum brilliantly. They've switched gears and how? Both have been finding boundaries at will and have put pressure right back on the visitors. After a disciplined start, the Bangladeshi spinners, particularly Rishad Hossain, has faltered with his lines and lengths, allowing India to ease the pressure. They need a wicket quickly after the break to stem the flow of runs. Shanto goes to his premier pacer, Mustafizur Rahman in search of a breakthrough.

Commentary.Commentary: A loud shout for LBW but the umpire remains unmoved! Mahmudullah is pretty convinced and he convinces Najmul Hossain Shanto to go for the review. The impact looked outside off there at first glance. Flicked from the side of the hand by Mahmudullah from over the wicket, full and around off, Nitish Kumar Reddy plants his front leg ahead and goes for the reverse. The ball goes under the bat and brushes Reddy's front pad. There is no bat involved on UltraEdge. The Ball Tracking shows that the ball turned enough to hit the off stump but the impact is umpire's call. A shake of the head by Mahmudullah as he walks back to his mark. The on-field decision is upheld but Bangladesh retain their review.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the action to begin in front of an expectant full house in Delhi. As is tradition at this venue, the ceremonial bell is rung before the start of play. The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by Najmul Hossain Shanto and his men. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson to open the innings for India. Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Mehidy Hasan. Away we go...

The captain of India, Suryakumar Yadav says that they were looking to bat first anyway. Tells that they had a chat with a couple of members of the ground staff who said there was dew late in the night. Further says that they want to challenge their bowlers with the wet ball. Shares that there is a lot of talent in their side. Adds that as a captain, it is important to stay one step ahead in this format. Opines that this looks like a very good surface. Mentions that they will look to start well and take it from there. Informs that they are unchanged for this game.

Najmul Hossain Shanto, the skipper of Bangladesh says that dew might come in later which is why he wants to bowl first. Adds that the wicket looks good and it has been a high-scoring venue and they will look to do well. On winning their last two games at this ground, he says it gives them a lot of confidence but this is a new day and they will have to give it their all and try to make the most of the first 6 overs. Concludes that they have one change with Shoriful Islam missing out and Tanzim Hasan Sakib coming in for him.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Parvez Hossain Emon, Litton Das (WK), Najmul Hossain Shanto (C), Towhid Hridoy, Mahmudullah, Jaker Ali, Mehidy Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman, Tanzim Hasan Sakib (In for Shoriful Islam).

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Sanju Samson (WK), Abhishek Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Nitish Kumar Reddy, Hardik Pandya, Riyan Parag, Rinku Singh, Washington Sundar, Varun Chakaravarthy, Arshdeep Singh, Mayank Yadav.
TOSS - Bangladesh have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Abhinav Mukund is out in the centre for the pitch analysis. He says the ground is not too big with the square boundaries being 55 meters and 63 meters while the straight boundary is 72 meters. Says that the pitch is hard and looks to be one of those surfaces where 200 might not be enough and could be a nightmare for the bowlers.

For Bangladesh, tonight is about redemption. Their batting struggled in the opener, managing just 127 runs, leaving the bowlers with little to defend. Captain Shanto will need to lead from the front, but a collective effort from the batters is essential if they hope to challenge India’s formidable attack. The spotlight will also be on their most-capped T20I player, Mahmudullah, who is set to retire from the format after this series. The visitors will be hoping to give him a fitting farewell by keeping the series alive and setting up a decider. Will Bangladesh find a way to bounce back, or will India seal the series tonight? Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

In the series opener in Gwalior, India outplayed Bangladesh in all departments. Their new-look squad hit the ground running, and Suryakumar Yadav and his men will look to carry that momentum forward, aiming to close out the series with another commanding performance. With their depth and balance, the hosts seem to have all their bases covered. They are likely to stick with the winning combination unless forced into changes by last-minute injuries, following the mantra - 'If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it'.

Hello and welcome from Delhi, where the Arun Jaitley Stadium sets the stage for the second T20I clash between India and Bangladesh. After suffering a bruising defeat in the series opener, Najmul Hossain Shanto’s side will be eager to prove their resilience and force a series decider. For India, a win tonight means sealing the series and extending their dominance at home. The Delhi surface, known for producing high-scoring matches as seen in the Indian T20 League, promises plenty of fireworks and an action-packed contest.
... MATCH DAY ...

The caravan now moves to the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi for the 2nd T20I between India and Bangladesh. After an engrossing Test series that the home side won 2-0 in fantastic fashion, the 1st T20I promised more of an even contest but Bangladesh were thumped by a great mix of youth and experience in the Indian lineup. The Bangla Tigers will be hoping to bounce back quickly in Delhi where we can expect a run-fest if recent matches are to go by and given how much cricket Bangladesh play at home, they aren't quite accustomed to flat pitches and lack a bit of power up the order and at the death to really score big. India on the other hand have no such issue as playing in the Indian T20 League has instilled a sense of fearlessness in the mind of this pretty young side. Talking about the first game, India put Bangladesh into bat on a decent-looking wicket but Arshdeep Singh was at his destructive best, knocking over both the openers to set the tone for the home side. The bowlers controlled the middle phase well enough and Varun Chakaravarthy picked up three wickets in total to make sure that Bangladesh couldn't build a big stand. Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mehidy Hasan were the only two batters to cross the 20-run mark with the latter really playing a lone hand towards the end. We also got to see spee-demon Mayank Yadav in action and he picked up a wicket on debut as well. The run chase though was a stark contrast to the first innings as India went berserk from the start. The openers were quick off the blocks and then the experienced likes of skipper Suryakumar Yadav and Hardik Pandya played a couple of quick cameos with the latter scoring 39 off just 16 balls as India chased down a target of 128 runs in just under 12 overs. Expect more aggressive cricket from India as they look to round off the series in Delhi itself and not leave things for the final game. Bangladesh will need to show some aggression of their own, especially with the bat and take India head on if they are to level the series. An engrossing contest is up on the cards, who are you backing?
